justifications.functional_suitability: Clinical Core Service addresses EMR and patient admissions, and Billing & Claims Service covers billing and insurance (R-01, R-03, R-04). However, appointment scheduling with resource clash checks (R-02) is only superficially referenced across Patient Portal App components without explicit clash-detection logic.
justifications.performance_efficiency: The sub-1s EMR load target (R-07) is well supported using Redis/RocksDB edge caches in Clinical Core Service, gRPC over mTLS, asynchronous RabbitMQ messaging in Billing & Claims Service, and Rate Limiting via Envoy/Redis in API Gateway.
justifications.compatibility: Interoperability (R-08) is thoroughly realized by Interoperability Engine featuring HAPI FHIR JPA Server, FHIR API Gateway & Validator, Apache Camel integration routing, and standard SMART-on-FHIR OAuth2 connections to External Lab & Imaging Systems.
justifications.usability: Patient Portal App provides a WCAG 2.1 AA accessible React SPA for Patients. However, dedicated interfaces or frontends for Clinicians and Administrative Staff (e.g., admissions, EMR workflows) are largely absent or conflated into backend components.
justifications.reliability: High availability (99.99% active-active, R-06) is directly enabled by Sync Orchestrator using Raft consensus, vector clocks in Conflict Resolver, edge caches in Clinical Core Service, and persistent DLQs in Interoperability Engine.
justifications.security: R-05, HIPAA, and GDPR are completely addressed via mTLS Istio service mesh, AES-256/TDE databases, Auth & Session Manager MFA, WAF, and tamper-evident audit log streaming to SIEM & Immutable Cold Storage across all services.
justifications.maintainability: Clear modular separation exists across containers (Clinical Core, Billing & Claims, Interoperability Engine). However, Clinical Core Service bundles admissions, workflows, and EMR together, while Sync Orchestrator also hosts an administrative dashboard backend, slightly blurring boundaries.
justifications.portability: Hybrid deployment (on-prem-k8s and eu-central-1) is well supported through containerization, Envoy proxies, edge caches (RocksDB/Redis), and Raft-based state sync, though specific multi-region Kubernetes configurations or cloud-specific deployment bindings remain mostly implicit.

PERF-01.justification: The architecture incorporates Redis and RocksDB edge caches within the Clinical Core Service to accelerate read paths. While API Gateway and local caching support sub-second P95 loads, heavy cache misses hitting PostgreSQL under concurrent morning spikes could present an unbenchmarked latency risk.
sensitivity_points: Edge cache hit ratio during concurrent clinical morning spikes
PostgreSQL connection pooling under burst query loads
tradeoffs: Increased memory overhead for local caching to achieve sub-second latency

PERF-02.justification: The Interoperability Engine decouples ingestion through HAPI FHIR, Apache Camel, and persistent Kafka/ActiveMQ messaging. This asynchronous queuing absorbs the 10,000-message burst within the target window without congesting the Clinical Core Service or degrading synchronous clinician read performance.
sensitivity_points: Message queue throughput and ingestion buffer capacity
Backpressure handling on internal gRPC sync to Clinical Core
tradeoffs: Temporary eventual consistency in EMR views during heavy asynchronous ingestion queues

AVAIL-01.justification: The architecture specifies a hybrid on-premises and eu-central-1 deployment coordinated by Sync Orchestrator with Raft and vector clocks. However, edge-level global DNS failover and ingress traffic re-routing mechanisms between regions are not explicitly detailed to guarantee the 1-minute failover SLA.
sensitivity_points: Raft consensus re-election time across hybrid network partitions
Replication lag between on-prem k8s and cloud database instances
tradeoffs: Active-active multi-region synchronization increases operational and conflict-resolution complexity

AVAIL-02.justification: Claim processing uses asynchronous RabbitMQ messaging, isolating client submissions from database failures. While message durability and the ledger component support retries, automated transaction idempotency and deduplication mechanisms during in-flight database failovers are not formally specified.
sensitivity_points: Idempotency token tracking across database reconnects
RabbitMQ message acknowledgment guarantees and broker failover latency
tradeoffs: Strict transactional consistency in ledger vs message processing throughput

MOD-01.justification: The modular architecture decouples billing and claims entirely from clinical systems. Adding an insurance clearinghouse only requires updating the Payment Processing or Claim Management components within the Billing & Claims Service, leaving the Clinical Core Service completely unaffected.
sensitivity_points: Decoupling of clearinghouse communication protocols from core ledger logic
tradeoffs: Custom clearinghouse adapters require maintaining distinct transformation modules

MOD-02.justification: Adding an audited demographic field is isolated to three components: Presentation Controller, BFF Router, and EMR Management Component. Auditing is captured automatically by the decoupled Audit Interceptor, allowing implementation and verification well within a single sprint.
sensitivity_points: Schema evolution rigidity across database models and API contracts
tradeoffs: End-to-end schema changes across presentation, BFF, and core service layers

SEC-01.justification: Authentication strictly requires multi-factor authentication via the external Identity Provider, validated at the API Gateway. Stolen passwords fail without the second factor, and failed authentication events are immediately emitted to SIEM and immutable cold storage for instant alerting.
sensitivity_points: Strict MFA enforcement policies configured at the central Identity Provider
Immediate latency of security event ingestion into the SIEM
tradeoffs: Enforcing multi-factor authentication increases authentication latency and user friction

SEC-02.justification: The architecture incorporates fine-grained ABAC/RBAC validation via token transformation and a dedicated Audit Interceptor within the Clinical Core Service. Every medical record access is intercepted and streamed as a tamper-evident audit log to SIEM & Immutable Cold Storage, satisfying the 10-year retention rule.
sensitivity_points: Coverage completeness of read interceptors across all EMR query paths
Cryptographic immutability and compliance retention settings of cold storage
tradeoffs: Synchronous audit interception introduces slight processing overhead on read operations
